claims.text: An optimal Cr concentration promotes rapid formation of a continuous, coherent Cr-rich oxide scale under high-temperature conditions.
The Cr-rich oxide scale consists primarily of CrNbO4 and Cr2O3.
A continuous Cr-rich oxide scale protects the alloy against high-temperature oxidation.
A continuous Cr-rich oxide scale protects the alloy against corrosion.
Formation of the protective Cr-rich oxide scale preserves mechanical strength.
Insufficient Cr produces an incomplete or discontinuous protective oxide scale.
Excess Cr induces adverse microstructural changes or instabilities that degrade strength.
The continuous Cr-rich oxide layer passivates the alloy surface and impedes ingress of oxygen and corrosive species.
Cr-rich protective oxides act as diffusion barriers.
At an optimal Cr concentration, protective oxides form quickly and uniformly.
The variant with an optimal Cr level will have lower oxidation weight gain than both the baseline and excessive-Cr variant.
The variant with an optimal Cr level will retain more tensile strength than both the baseline and excessive-Cr variant.
The variant with an optimal Cr level will have lower corrosion current density than both the baseline and excessive-Cr variant.
The protective oxides may cease to be stable above approximately 1100 °C.
Inhomogeneous Cr distribution may prevent the expected improvements in strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
Preliminary studies can be used to identify an optimized Cr content.

contradictions.description: The proposed scale is said to contain CrNbO4, but Al0.3FeCoNi is offered as a possible baseline and contains no Nb; because the intervention adds only Cr, that listed comparison cannot form CrNbO4 unless an unstated Nb addition is made.
